project: Build Your Own DNS Ad/Tracker Blocker
summary: A TypeScript library (zero runtime dependencies) implementing a Pi-hole-style DNS proxy that sinkholes ad/tracker domains and forwards everything else to a configured upstream resolver, with TTL-respecting caching, built in one stage as a self-contained extension of this repo's existing 15-dns-resolver project (reusing its proven design ideas -- wire format basics, the TC-bit-to-TCP retry pattern, the stub-server-on-a-high-port test setup -- without depending on its package). The single biggest design decision is relaying forwarded upstream answers as raw bytes rather than re-encoding them: this proxy only decodes what it needs to make a decision (the header, the question, and for an upstream reply, each answer's name/type/class/ttl, with rdata skipped by its length and never interpreted), because an undecoded rdata field (CNAME, NS, MX, SOA, PTR, ...) can contain a DNS-compressed name whose pointer is only valid relative to the exact bytes of the packet it was written into -- rebuilding a new packet and copying that rdata unchanged could silently corrupt the pointer. The blocklist is a trie over reversed dot-labels (chosen over a Set of domain strings because a Set needs one fresh string allocation and hash per ancestor of the query name on every lookup, while the trie walks the query's own labels once and shares memory across the huge numbers of subdomains a real tracker list has). Block responses support two configurable modes -- NXDOMAIN (technically correct, but some clients retry aggressively on it) or a sinkhole A record (a lie that most clients treat as final) -- mirroring Pi-hole's own real, unresolved design debate; sinkholing is implemented only for A queries, with NXDOMAIN for every other type in both modes. The cache uses lazy expiry (no background sweep, same philosophy as this repo's 23-password-manager session idle timeout) and stores raw bytes plus the byte offsets of each answer's TTL field, so a cache hit can hand back a TTL counted down by elapsed time rather than a stale original value -- safe specifically because a TTL is a fixed-position 4-byte integer with no name compression nearby, unlike the rdata this project deliberately never touches. The threat model is deliberately narrower than 15-dns-resolver's iterative resolver (which talks to arbitrary, never-before-seen authoritative servers and must defend every query with randomized source port and ID against Kaminsky-style spoofing): this proxy only ever round-trips with one configured, trusted upstream, so it keeps one cheap check (a reply must come from the configured upstream's exact address/port) without reproducing the full defense. Upstream forwarding is UDP with a timeout, TC-bit-triggered TCP retry, and SERVFAIL (never a hang or crash) on timeout, error, or a reply whose transaction id/QR bit does not match what was sent. 89 tests total, including a randomized invariant test (5 seeds, 400 queries each, checked against a hand-tracked shadow model of what should be cached and when it expires). Mutation checks: 23 total, 20 caught on the first run, 3 real gaps found and closed (a reserved DNS label-type check only incidentally covered by an unrelated bounds check; a wrong-source-address defense never actually exercised by any test, closed via a test-only onUdpBound hook letting a rogue socket race the real upstream; upstream reply id/QR verification never violated by any existing stub, closed with a new wrong-id stub behavior) -- all 23 now caught. Not built: AAAA/other-type sinkholing, DNS presentation escapes, downstream TCP, negative caching, config hot-reload, multiple blocklists/allowlists, query logging, rate limiting beyond a loopback-only bind guard.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek Pi-hole-jaisa DNS ad/tracker blocker banaya hai, TypeScript mein, zero runtime dependencies. Yeh blocklisted domains ko khud answer karta hai (NXDOMAIN ya ek sinkhole IP, configurable), aur baaki sab kuch ek configured upstream resolver ko forward karta hai, TTL-respecting caching ke saath. Sabse bada design decision: forwarded answers ko RAW BYTES mein relay karna, re-encode kabhi nahi -- isse DNS name-compression pointer corruption bachta hai. Blocklist ek trie hai reversed labels par, Set se zyada efficient large lists ke liye. 89 tests, 23 mutation checks, sab caught.
pitch.explain_2min:
Yeh project '15-dns-resolver' ka natural extension hai -- same wire format basics, same TC-bit-to-TCP retry pattern, same stub-server-on-high-port test setup, par alag job: resolve karna nahi, relay karna, except ek blocklist ke against check karna.

Sabse bada design decision yeh hai: forwarded upstream answers ko RAW BYTES mein relay karna, kabhi re-encode nahi karna. Yeh '15-dns-resolver' se different choice hai (jo pura decode-and-re-encode karta hai apne stub clients ke liye). Yahan proxy sirf itna decode karta hai jitna decision lene ke liye zaroori hai -- header, question, aur upstream answer ka name/type/class/ttl, rdata ko length se skip karke, kabhi interpret nahi. Reason: ek undecoded rdata (CNAME, NS, MX, ...) ke andar ek DNS-compressed name ho sakta hai jiska pointer sirf EXACT original packet bytes ke relative valid hai -- naya packet banate waqt yeh rdata copy karna silently corrupt kar sakta hai.

Blocklist ek trie hai reversed dot-labels par, Set nahi -- Set ko har ancestor ke liye ek fresh string allocation+hash chahiye hota, trie query ke labels ek baar walk karta hai aur shared suffixes (jaise hazaaron doubleclick.net subdomains) memory share karte hain.

Block response do modes support karta hai -- NXDOMAIN (technically correct) ya ek sinkhole IP (jo clients ko kam retry karata hai) -- Pi-hole ka apna real, unresolved design debate.

Cache lazy expiry use karta hai, background sweep nahi (23-password-manager ke session idle timeout jaisi hi philosophy), aur TTL ko elapsed time se count down karta hai cache hit par.

Threat model deliberately NARROWER hai 15-dns-resolver se -- yeh sirf ek configured, trusted upstream se baat karta hai, poore internet se nahi, isliye Kaminsky-style full spoofing defence reproduce nahi hoti, sirf ek cheap source-address check. 89 tests, 23 mutation checks, sab caught.
pitch.deep_5min:
Ek query ki journey, ek blocked domain, ek allowed domain, aur ek cache hit.

Setup. SinkholeServer ek UDP socket bind karta hai (default port 15353, 53 nahi -- root chahiye hota 53 ke liye). BlockList config/blocklist.txt se load hota hai -- har line ek trie mein jaati hai, reversed labels ke order mein (jaise 'ads.example.com' -> com -> example -> ads nodes).

Blocked query. Client 'tracker.ads.example.com' ke liye A record poochta hai. SinkholeProxy.handle() pehle query decode karta hai (header + question, wire.ts se), phir BlockList.isBlocked() check karta hai -- yeh query ke labels ko reverse order mein trie mein walk karta hai, aur 'ads.example.com' node tak pahunch ke dekhta hai yeh ek 'blocked' node hai. Match milta hai -- upstream ko CONTACT kiye bina, proxy khud ek response banata hai (buildBlockResponse): 'nxdomain' mode mein NXDOMAIN, 'sinkhole' mode mein ek configured A record (default 0.0.0.0). stats.blocked increment hota hai.

Allowed query. Client 'news.example.com' poochta hai. isBlocked() false return karta hai. Proxy pehle cache check karta hai (name, type) key se -- miss. forwardQuery() ek fresh UDP socket banata hai, upstream (jaise 1.1.1.1) ko exact query forward karta hai, client ka apna transaction id use karte hue. Upstream se reply aata hai -- decodeResponse() ISKA sirf header+question+answers ka name/type/class/ttl decode karta hai, rdata ko LENGTH se skip karta hai bina interpret kiye (yeh crucial hai: agar rdata mein ek compressed name pointer ho, aur hum naya packet banate waqt usse copy kar dete bina samjhe, pointer WRONG offset point kar sakta tha naye packet mein). Proxy upstream ke RAW BYTES relay karta hai client ko, sirf 2-byte transaction ID patch karke (client ka apna id, upstream ka nahi). Response cache hoti hai (name, type) key se, smallest TTL answers mein se, saath mein har TTL field ka BYTE OFFSET bhi store hota hai.

Cache hit. Client dobara 'news.example.com' poochta hai, TTL window ke andar. Cache hit milta hai -- upstream ko call hi nahi kiya jaata (stub ka call count unchanged). TTL field ka stored offset use karke, response ki copy mein TTL ko elapsed time se COUNT DOWN kiya jaata hai (jaise 300 se 290), ek fresh client transaction id patch kiya jaata hai, aur relay ho jaata hai -- bilkul ek real resolver ka cache jaisa behavior.

TC bit aur SERVFAIL. Agar upstream ka UDP reply truncated ho (TC=1), forwardQuery() SAME query TCP par retry karta hai, full answer leta hai, usi ko relay aur cache karta hai. Agar upstream time out ho jaaye ya ek mismatched id/QR wala reply bheje, client ko SERVFAIL milta hai promptly -- kabhi hang nahi, kabhi crash nahi, aur kabhi galat answer relay nahi hota.

Threat model. 15-dns-resolver poore internet ke arbitrary authoritative servers se baat karta hai -- har query ko random source port AND random ID se defend karna padta hai (Kaminsky spoofing). Yeh proxy sirf EK configured upstream se baat karta hai -- isliye sirf ek cheap check kaafi hai: reply configured upstream ke exact address/port se aana chahiye, warna ignore (yahan tak ki ek rogue socket race kare real upstream se pehle, toh bhi ignore hota hai).
pitch.architecture_walkthrough: src/wire.ts: header+question decode, minimal answer-TTL decode (rdata skip by length), small-message encode (sirf A records, jo sinkhole mode banata hai). src/blocklist.ts: trie-based BlockList, plain-text blocklist parsing/loading. src/cache.ts: raw-bytes ResponseCache, TTL expiry (lazy, no sweep) aur TTL countdown on read, maxEntries oldest-first eviction. src/clock.ts: injectable Clock (systemClock/ManualClock), same shape as 22-messaging. src/transport.ts: ek forwarded query to upstream -- UDP with timeout, TC->TCP retry. src/proxy.ts: SinkholeProxy -- decision logic (block / cache hit / forward), pure buffer in, buffer out, testable without sockets. src/server.ts: SinkholeServer -- real UDP listener clients talk to, defaults to port 15353, loopback-only unless allowNonLoopback. src/stub-upstream.ts: ek fully controllable fake upstream, tests AND demo dono use karte hain. src/demo.ts: npm run demo -- ek block, ek forward, ek cache hit, ek TC->TCP retry. config/blocklist.txt: ek small illustrative blocklist. test/: 7 files -- wire (24), blocklist (14), cache (11), transport (3), server (6), proxy (26), invariant (5 seeds randomized).
difficult_decisions: Forwarded answers RAW BYTES mein relay karna, kabhi re-encode nahi. Yeh single biggest decision hai, aur 15-dns-resolver se DIFFERENT choice hai (jo poora decode-re-encode karta hai). Reason: undecoded rdata (CNAME, NS, MX, ...) mein ek DNS-compressed name pointer ho sakta hai jo sirf ORIGINAL packet bytes ke relative valid hai -- naya packet banate waqt yeh silently corrupt ho sakta tha.

Blocklist ek trie over reversed dot-labels, Set of domain strings nahi. Set ko har ancestor ke liye fresh string+hash chahiye; trie query ke labels ek baar walk karta hai, shared suffixes (jaise hazaaron doubleclick.net subdomains) memory share karte hain -- cheaper exactly us input shape par jo real tracker list ki hoti hai.

Block response: NXDOMAIN ya sinkhole IP, configurable, hardcoded nahi. Pi-hole ka apna real design debate -- NXDOMAIN technically correct hai par kuch clients aggressively retry karte hain usme, sinkhole IP ek lie hai par zyada clients usse 'final' maan lete hain. Sinkholing sirf A queries ke liye, baaki types NXDOMAIN dono modes mein.

Cache lazy expiry, background sweep nahi -- 23-password-manager ke session idle timeout jaisi hi reasoning: sweep timer ko apna lifecycle (kaun start/stop kare, kis clock se) chahiye hota, benefit ke bagair extra design/test cost.

Threat model DELIBERATELY narrower hai 15-dns-resolver se -- yeh sirf EK configured, trusted upstream se baat karta hai (jaise 1.1.1.1 Pi-hole ke liye), poore internet ke arbitrary servers se nahi -- isliye full Kaminsky-spoofing defence (random source port+ID) reproduce nahi hoti, sirf ek cheap source-address check.
biggest_challenges: WIRE5 mutation survivor: reserved label-type (0x40/0x80) check removal pehle PASS ho gaya tha kyunki existing test mein not-enough-trailing-bytes bhi tha, toh ek UNRELATED truncation check usse pehle hi catch kar leta tha -- reserved-type check khud kabhi exercise nahi hua. Naya test banaya: ek 0x40 label ke saath 64 REAL bytes following (koi bounds check kabhi fire hi nahi karega) -- sirf reserved-type check isse reject kar sakta hai.

TRANSPORT1 mutation survivor: har test ka 'upstream' ekmaatra responder tha, isliye wrong-source-address check ke paas kabhi KUCH filter karne ko tha hi nahi. Isse honestly close karne ke liye apna khud ka ephemeral UDP source port MODULE SE BAHAR seekhna zaroori tha -- ek test-only ForwardOptions.onUdpBound hook add kiya, bind hone ke turant baad fire hota hai, real query bhejne se PEHLE. Naya test: ek rogue socket is hook se ek PEHLE-hi fully-formed spoofed answer bhejta hai, real upstream se bhi pehle -- real answer phir bhi jeetta hai.

PROXY3 mutation survivor: stub upstream hamesha well-behaved tha (correct id, QR=1), isliye id/QR check kabhi 'right answer vs wrong answer' ke beech khada nahi tha kisi test mein. Naya stub behavior 'wrong-id' banaya (ek confused upstream jo (id+1) se answer deta hai), plus ek test jo assert karta hai client ko SERVFAIL milta hai APNE OWN id ke saath, mismatched answer kabhi nahi.
failure_scenarios: Upstream timeout ya unreachable: client ko SERVFAIL milta hai promptly, kabhi hang nahi, kabhi process crash nahi, aur response cache nahi hota.
Upstream reply ka transaction id ya QR bit mismatch kare: SERVFAIL, relay nahi hota -- confused ya buggy upstream ka galat answer client tak kabhi nahi pahunchta.
Koi rogue socket ek spoofed answer bhej de real upstream se PEHLE: wrong-source-address check isse ignore karta hai, real upstream ka answer hi use hota hai.
Upstream UDP reply truncated (TC=1): SAME query TCP par retry hoti hai, full answer liya jaata hai, usi ko relay aur cache kiya jaata hai.
Query malformed ho (12 bytes se kam, galat opcode, galat class, 0 ya 2+ questions): closest real-DNS response milta hai (drop, FORMERR, ya NOTIMP), crash kabhi nahi.
Cache ka TTL window elapse ho jaaye (ManualClock.advance): next query automatically upstream ko call karta hai, fresh TTL ke saath cache replace hoti hai.
improvements: AAAA ya kisi bhi doosre record type ka sinkholing abhi nahi hai -- sinkhole mode sirf A queries answer karta hai, baaki NXDOMAIN dono modes mein.
DNS presentation escapes (\DDD, \.) support nahi hain -- ek label jisme literal '.' byte ho, mis-split ho sakta hai re-encode karte waqt (real hostnames mein yeh kabhi nahi hota).
Downstream TCP nahi hai -- clients sirf UDP se yeh proxy reach kar sakte hain; TCP sirf proxy khud upstream se baat karte waqt use karta hai.
Negative caching nahi hai -- ek NXDOMAIN ya NODATA upstream se relay hota hai par kabhi cache nahi hota, next identical query phir upstream ko jaati hai.
Config hot-reload, multiple blocklists with precedence, allowlist exceptions, ya query logging/stats page (beyond in-memory counters) abhi nahi hain.

Rate limiting ya abuse protection nahi hai proxy ke apne listener par, sirf loopback-only bind guard hai -- same reasoning jo 15-dns-resolver ke stub server mein hai (open resolver DNS amplification tool ban sakta hai).

learning_path.concept: Why relay raw bytes instead of re-encoding a forwarded answer
steps: 1. Concept: yeh proxy sirf header, question, aur ek upstream answer ka name/type/class/ttl decode karta hai -- rdata ko uski LENGTH se skip karta hai, kabhi interpret nahi. Jo bhi yeh RELAY karta hai woh upstream ke EXACT bytes hote hain, sirf 2-byte transaction id patched.

2. Project need: ek undecoded rdata (CNAME, NS, MX, SOA, PTR...) ke andar ek DNS-compressed name ho sakta hai jiska compression pointer SIRF original packet ke bytes ke relative valid hai. Naya packet banate waqt (alag header, shayad alag question encoding) yeh rdata unchanged copy karna pointer ko WRONG offset bana sakta hai -- silent corruption.
3. Code/API: src/wire.ts decodeResponse (rdata skipped by rdlength, never decoded); src/proxy.ts handle (relay logic, cache-hit id patching).
4. Detail: sirf cache hit par 2-byte transaction ID aur fixed-position TTL fields patch hote hain -- dono plain integers hain, koi name compression nearby nahi.
5. Demo: cd projects/25-dns-sinkhole && npx vitest run test/wire.test.ts -t 'skipping rdata untouched' -- 'reads a compressed answer name..., skipping rdata untouched'.
6. Interviewer next: agar kabhi full RR decoding add karni ho (jaise ek allowlist feature jo CNAME follow kare), kya naye risks introduce honge?

learning_path.concept: The blocklist trie: exact-domain and wildcard-subdomain blocking
steps: 1. Concept: BlockList ek trie hai reversed dot-labels par. Ek domain block karna uski entire subtree block karta hai (saari subdomains), kabhi parent ya sibling nahi.

2. Project need: ek Set of domain strings har ancestor ke liye ek fresh string allocation+hash chahta -- ek real blocklist mein thousands of subdomains ek common tracker domain ke, trie unka suffix SHARE karta hai, ek baar hi.
3. Code/API: src/blocklist.ts BlockList.add, isBlocked, labelsOf.
4. Detail: case-insensitive, trailing dot ignored; ek SHORTER listed domain ka subtree ek LONGER query ko cover karta hai, insertion order se independent.
5. Demo: cd projects/25-dns-sinkhole && npx vitest run test/blocklist.test.ts -- the core block-matching tests.
6. Interviewer next: agar million-domain blocklist ho, trie ka memory footprint Set se kitna alag hoga?

learning_path.concept: NXDOMAIN vs a sinkhole IP: Pi-hole's own real design debate
steps: 1. Concept: block response do configurable modes support karta hai -- NXDOMAIN ('yeh naam exist nahi karta') ya ek sinkhole A record (ek lie, par normal-dikhne-wala answer).

2. Project need: NXDOMAIN technically correct hai, par kuch client software ise 'try again' samajh ke aggressively retry karta hai -- ek blocked ad request ko retries ke burst mein badal deta. Sinkhole IP ek lie hai par zyada clients normal answer ko final maan lete hain.
3. Code/API: src/proxy.ts buildBlockResponse; SinkholeProxyOptions.mode/sinkholeAddress.
4. Detail: sinkholing SIRF A queries ke liye implement hai; har doosra query type (AAAA, MX, ...) NXDOMAIN paata hai DONO modes mein.
5. Demo: cd projects/25-dns-sinkhole && npx vitest run test/proxy.test.ts -t 'block modes' -- 'non-A types get NXDOMAIN in sinkhole mode too'.
6. Interviewer next: AAAA sinkholing add karna (:: address se) kitna bada change hoga -- kahan isolate hoga?

learning_path.concept: TTL caching: lazy expiry and counting down on read
steps: 1. Concept: ResponseCache raw bytes PLUS har TTL field ka byte offset store karta hai. get() TTL ko ELAPSED TIME se count down karta hai, floor zero par.
2. Project need: ek cache hit ko stale original TTL nahi dena chahiye -- 10 second baad ek 300-second TTL entry ko 290 dikhana chahiye, real resolver jaisa behavior.
3. Code/API: src/cache.ts ResponseCache.put, get; src/clock.ts injectable Clock.
4. Detail: yeh safe hai specifically kyunki TTL ek fixed-position 4-byte integer hai, koi name compression nearby nahi -- unlike rdata jo yeh project kabhi touch nahi karta.
5. Demo: cd projects/25-dns-sinkhole && npx vitest run test/cache.test.ts -t 'countdown' -- TTL countdown test, including right at the edge of expiry.
6. Interviewer next: agar do clients SAME query karen slightly different times par, dono ko kya TTL dikhna chahiye?

learning_path.concept: A narrower threat model: one trusted upstream, not the open internet
steps: 1. Concept: 15-dns-resolver arbitrary authoritative servers se baat karta hai aur Kaminsky-style spoofing defend karta hai (random source port AND random ID). Yeh proxy sirf EK configured upstream se baat karta hai.
2. Project need: ek narrower threat model ek narrower defence justify karta hai -- yahan sirf EK cheap check zaroori hai: reply configured upstream ke exact address/port se aana chahiye.
3. Code/API: src/transport.ts queryUdp (source-address check), ForwardOptions.onUdpBound (test-only hook).
4. Detail: ID/QR match ek doosre layer par check hota hai (proxy.ts mein, decoded reply par) -- mismatch SERVFAIL deta hai, relay nahi karta.
5. Demo: cd projects/25-dns-sinkhole && npx vitest run test/transport.test.ts -t 'different address' -- 'ignores a reply from a different address/port...'.
6. Interviewer next: agar yeh proxy kabhi arbitrary upstream servers se baat karne lage (jaise iterative resolution add karke), threat model kaise badlega?

learning_path.concept: Robustness: malformed queries and SERVFAIL instead of crashing
steps: 1. Concept: ek query jo proxy samajh nahi paata, closest real-DNS answer paata hai -- 12 bytes se kam drop, galat opcode/class NOTIMP, 0 ya 2+ questions FORMERR, QR=1 wala packet (response, query nahi) silently drop.

2. Project need: ek untrusted network se aane wala har byte adversarial ho sakta hai -- proxy ko kabhi crash nahi karna chahiye, aur do misconfigured servers ek doosre ka output 'ping-pong' kabhi nahi karni chahiye.
3. Code/API: src/wire.ts decodeQuery (bounds checks, WireError); src/proxy.ts handle (opcode/class/question-count validation).
4. Detail: Reader class ka har read bounds-checked hai; 1500 random + 500 bit-flipped packets 5 seeds ke across test hote hain.
5. Demo: cd projects/25-dns-sinkhole && npx vitest run test/proxy.test.ts -t 'malformed' -- malformed and unusual queries tests.
6. Interviewer next: QR=1 drop check hatane se exact kya scenario ban sakta hai do misconfigured DNS servers ke beech?

learning_path.concept: Testing honestly: mutation testing and finding exercises that look covered but are not
steps: 1. Concept: ek deliberate break apply karo, suite chalao, dekho test fail hota hai ya nahi, file restore karo. Ek 'caught' result bhi misleading ho sakta hai agar woh check KISI DOOSRE check se accidentally overlap karta ho.
2. Project need: '89 tests pass' yeh nahi batata ki har individual guard genuinely exercise ho rahi hai -- WIRE5 ka survivor exactly isi gap ko dikhata hai.
3. Code/API: test/invariant.test.ts (randomized, 5 seeds x 400 queries), README.md ki mutation table.

4. Detail: 23 mutation checks, 20 first-run caught, 3 genuine gaps the (WIRE5: reserved label-type check sirf incidentally covered by an unrelated bounds check; TRANSPORT1: wrong-source check kabhi exercise nahi hua kyunki koi test mein doosra sender nahi tha; PROXY3: id/QR verification kabhi violated nahi hui kisi stub se) -- teeno precise new tests se close kiye gaye.
5. Demo: cd projects/25-dns-sinkhole && npm test (89 tests), aur npx vitest run test/invariant.test.ts.
6. Interviewer next: ek check jo 'caught' dikh raha hai kisi UNRELATED reason se, aise case ko kaise systematically dhoondhte?
